notes: The tutorial's 'Arduino Leonardo, Micro, or Due' board was matched to the catalogue's arduino-leonardo, which is the board drawn in the circuit image.

The button straddles the breadboard centre gap. Its top legs are in columns 4 and 6 of the rows f-j half, and its bottom legs are in columns 4 and 6 of the rows a-e half. Following the catalogue, rows f-j are bank 'b' and rows a-e are bank 't', although the image draws rows j-f at the top.

Blue wire: Leonardo pin 2 to column 6, row i, which is the same strip as the button's top (side 1) legs. Black wire: Leonardo GND to column 4, row c, which is the same strip as the button's bottom (side 2) legs. Pressing the button joins D2 to GND.
No external resistor is used. The sketch enables INPUT_PULLUP on pin 2.
The Leonardo has several GND pins, and the image shows the wire on the highlighted GND in the left header. This was mapped to GND.1.
The image shows the rail pins unused, so no power-rail connections were made.
